body.p: Claims 1-20 will be pending after entry of the present paper. Claims 1, 8, 10, 13, 15, and 19 are amended. Support for the amendments may be found in the originally filed specification, drawings, and claims. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of this application in view of the amendments and remarks submitted herein.

p.u: uest for Consideration in the AFCP 2.0 Program

body.p: Applicant requests this application to be considered in the AFCP 2.0 program. Applicant believes this response to be compliant with the requirements of 78 Fed. Reg. 29117. Specifically, Applicant submits form PTO/SB/434 with this reply, Applicant asserts that at least one independent claim is amended that does not broaden the scope, and Applicant is willing and available to participate in any interview initiated by the examiner concerning the amendments and remarks herein.

The Office Action rejects claims 1-5, 9-11, 14-16 and 20 under 35 U.S.C. @ 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by U.S. Patent Publication No. 2020/0 164988 to Alvarez ("Alvarez"). The Office Action rejects claims 6, 7, 12, 17 and 18 under 35 U.S.C. @ 103 as being obvious over Alvarez in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 20 18/0369434 to Callahan ("Callahan"). The Office Action rejects claims 8, 13 and 19 under 35 U.S.C. @ 103 as being obvious over Alvarez in view of Callahan with respect to the health status of a system using UV lights as applied to claims 6, 12 and 17 above, and further in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2008/013 1332 to Nguyen ("Nguyen"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.

"[T]he hallmark of anticipation is prior invention" and "the prior art reference - in order to anticipate under 35 U.S.C. @ 102 - must not only disclose all elements of the claim within the four comers of the document, but must also disclose those elements arranged as in the claim." NetMoneyln, Inc. v. VeriSign, Inc., 545 F.3d 1359, 1369 (Fed. Cir. 2008). Applicant respectfully submits that the claims as amended are not anticipated.

Claim 1 is amended to recite "a central controller coupled to the plurality of touchiess sensors, the actuator, and the light source, the central controller configured to make an inference as to a portion of the lavatory that was used based on the data received from each of

the plurality of touchless sensors and to control at least one of the actuator and the light source based on the inference, wherein the central controller is further configured to determine a health status of the system, the health status including a remaining life of the ultraviolet light source, and to control the ultraviolet light source further based on the health status." Alvarez does not teach or disclose each and every element of amended claim 1. The cited references, either along or in combination, fail to disclose or contemplate each and every element of amended claim 1. The Office Action states that Alvarez in view of Callahan "does not disclose the alternative of 'or a remaining quantity of supplies in the lavatory"' and instead relies on Nguyen. That is, the Office Action relies on Nguyen for teaching "a remaining quantity of supplies in the lavatory." However, Nguyen fails to disclose or contemplate at least "the central controller is further configured to determine a health status of the system, the health status including a remaining life of the ultraviolet light source." Similarly, Callahan fails to disclose or contemplate at least "the central controller is further configured to determine a health status of the system, the health status including a remaining life of the ultraviolet light source." Furthermore, the Office Action has not shown how the cited references, either alone or in combination, disclose or contemplate at least "the central controller is further configured to determine a health status of the system, the health status including a remaining life of the ultraviolet light source" as recited by amended claim. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claim 1 be reconsidered and withdrawn.

Claims 10 and 15 are amended similar to claim 1 and are therefore patentable for at least the same reasons discussed above. Claims 2-9, 11-14, and 16-20 depend from claims 1, 10, and 105 respectively, and are patentable for at least the same reasons as discussed above, further in view of their own respective features. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 1- 20 be reconsidered and withdrawn.

In view of the above remarks and amendments, Applicant respectfully submits that all pending claims are in condition for allowance. The Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned at the Examiner's convenience, if doing so will further prosecution of the subject application.
